title: Finite-mode light–matter models and detection statistics

items.title: Finite-mode dipole and detector assignment
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
**(a) Finite oscillator-mode data.** Choose an integer $M\ge1$, the one-particle mode space $\mathfrak h=\mathbb C^M$ with a declared orthonormal mode basis $e_1,\ldots,e_M$, and the bosonic Fock space $\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathfrak h^{\otimes_s n}$ with vacuum $\Omega$. Here $\mathfrak h^{\otimes_s n}$ is the range of the orthogonal symmetrizer in the completed $n$-fold Hilbert tensor product, with the zero-particle sector $\mathbb C\Omega$. For $\mathbf n=(n_1,\ldots,n_M)\in\mathbb N_0^M$, let $|\mathbf n\rangle$ be the normalized occupation vector. Define the finite-particle subspace $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}:=\{\psi=(\psi^{(n)})_{n\ge0}\in\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h):\psi^{(n)}=0\text{ for all but finitely many }n\}=\operatorname{span}\{|\mathbf n\rangle:\mathbf n\in\mathbb N_0^M\}$. The mode operators are dimensionless and on $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}$ satisfy $a_j|\mathbf n\rangle=\sqrt{n_j}|\mathbf n-\mathbf e_j\rangle$ and $a_j^*|\mathbf n\rangle=\sqrt{n_j+1}|\mathbf n+\mathbf e_j\rangle$, with the first expression zero if $n_j=0$. The Fock space is infinite-dimensional for each $M\ge1$; no particle-number cutoff or tensor factorization of an individual photon into position and spin is part of this assignment.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and countable choice wherever the finite-mode Fock, quadrature, and implementability suppliers require them. These are mathematical hypotheses of the assignment, not physical postulates.

**Mode-frequency data.** Use $\hbar>0$ for the reduced Planck constant in joule-seconds under the framework's SI convention. For each selected mode $j$, choose a positive angular frequency $\omega_j>0$ in seconds$^{-1}$; the assigned one-quantum energy scale is $\hbar\omega_j$ joules. These are parameters of the finite-mode model, not measured frequencies.

**(b) Finite atom and dipole data.** Choose $d\ge1$, an atomic Hilbert space $\mathcal H_A=\mathbb C^d$, a Hermitian atomic energy matrix $H_A$ in joules, Hermitian compressed dipole matrices $D_j$ in coulomb-metres, and real mode field scales $\mathcal E_j$ in volts per metre. The matrix elements of $G_j:=\mathcal E_jD_j/\hbar$ have units seconds$^{-1}$, where $\hbar>0$ is retained in joule-seconds. The finite matrices and scales are chosen model data. If they are obtained by compressing a larger atomic model, that compression's error is a separate model input and is not bounded here.

Write $\mathcal H_{AF}:=\mathcal H_A\widehat\otimes\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)$ for the completed ordered Hilbert tensor product, with the atom factor first, and let $\kappa:\mathcal H_A\odot\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)\to\mathcal H_{AF}$ be the canonical isometric inclusion. Let $I_A$ and $I_F$ denote the identity operators on $\mathcal H_A$ and $\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)$. Let $\mathcal D_0:=\kappa[\mathcal H_A\odot\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}]\subseteq\mathcal H_{AF}$ be the algebraic product domain. If $f_1,\ldots,f_d$ is the standard orthonormal basis of $\mathcal H_A=\mathbb C^d$, then the vectors $\kappa(f_\alpha\otimes|\mathbf n\rangle)$ form a complete orthonormal basis by the Hilbert tensor product and finite-mode Fock product-basis conclusions for this ordered pair. Hence $\mathcal D_0$ is dense in $\mathcal H_{AF}$.

The assigned dipole interaction is the linear operator $V_{\mathrm{dip}}:\mathcal D_0\to\mathcal H_{AF}$ defined on elementary tensors by $V_{\mathrm{dip}}(\kappa(\phi\otimes\psi)):=-\sum_{j=1}^{M}\mathcal E_j\kappa(D_j\phi\otimes(a_j+a_j^*)\psi)$ for $\phi\in\mathcal H_A$ and $\psi\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}$, and extended linearly to $\mathcal D_0$. Each map $(\phi,\psi)\mapsto\kappa(D_j\phi\otimes(a_j+a_j^*)\psi)$ is bilinear, so it descends to the algebraic tensor product; $a_j,a_j^*$ preserve $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}$. Each summand has units joules. This is the declared algebraic product domain of the finite-core expression; no graph-core assertion for a closed realization is made. The assignment does not assert that an arbitrary such sum has a self-adjoint realization or generates an evolution; any dynamical use must state and justify its operator domain. The Jaynes–Cummings supplier below gives one specific self-adjoint direct-sum realization.

**(c) Mode transformations.** A finite mode-coordinate change is assigned only when its finite Bogoliubov matrices satisfy the exact hypotheses of the finite-mode implementability statement: for $U,V\in M_M(\mathbb C)$, $UU^*-VV^*=I_M$ and $UV^T=VU^T$. The resulting unitary acts on this finite-mode Fock space. The statement assumes the Axiom of Choice; this is a mathematical assumption, not a physical law. No infinite-mode implementability follows.

**(d) Detector outcome models.** A detector's outcome space $(X,\Sigma)$ and POVM $E:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(\mathcal H_{AF})$ are declared model data: each $E(B)$ is bounded and positive, $E(X)=I$, and $E$ is countably additive in the weak operator topology. For a density operator $\rho$ on $\mathcal H_{AF}$ (a positive trace-class operator of trace one), the assigned probability is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ under the framework's stated measurement convention. An ideal number-resolving model on the field has outcomes $\mathbf n\in\mathbb N_0^M$ and effects $I_A\otimes|\mathbf n\rangle\langle\mathbf n|$; these are bounded tensor maps and projections on $\mathcal H_{AF}$ by the tensor-map adjoint and composition rules. For ideal homodyne of mode $j$ at phase $\theta\in\mathbb R$, let $R_j(\theta)|\mathbf n\rangle=e^{i\theta n_j}|\mathbf n\rangle$ and $X_{j,\theta}:=\hbar^{-1/2}R_j(\theta)Q_jR_j(\theta)^*$, where $\mathcal U:\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C^M)\to L^2(\mathbb R^M)$ is the Fock-to-Schrödinger unitary and $Q_j:=\mathcal U^{-1}M_{\sqrt\hbar x_j}\mathcal U$. Here $M_{\sqrt\hbar x_j}$ multiplies by $\sqrt\hbar x_j$ on its maximal domain $\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R^M):x_jf\in L^2(\mathbb R^M)\}$. Thus $X_{j,\theta}$ is self-adjoint by unitary conjugation and on $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}$ equals $(e^{-i\theta}a_j+e^{i\theta}a_j^*)/\sqrt2$. Its spectral PVM $B\mapsto I_A\otimes\mathbf1_B(X_{j,\theta})$ is defined by the same bounded tensor maps and is the ideal homodyne POVM on the product space. These are ideal outcome assignments, not claims about a detector's optical local oscillator, efficiency, bandwidth, calibration or state update. If a state update or a finite detector environment is modeled, declare its instrument separately. The finite product-preparation/unitary/partial-trace assignment described by the finite open-system postulate is for $H_S=\mathbb C^d$ and $H_E=\mathbb C^m$ with a fixed environment state and a declared joint unitary; it may be used for a separately selected finite-dimensional subsystem but does not cover the Fock field. A reduced-dynamics model involving the Fock field must separately specify a trace-class joint preparation and joint unitary on $\mathcal H_{AF}$. The trace-class partial trace $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)}:\mathcal S_1(\mathcal H_{AF})\to\mathcal S_1(\mathcal H_A)$ is defined for arbitrary Hilbert factors, is trace-norm contractive, and preserves positivity and trace by the mathematical partial-trace result listed below. No Fock-field reduced dynamics or reservoir limit is adopted here.

**(e) Optional approximation regimes.** A long-wavelength identification with a spatial electromagnetic mode requires a separately declared atomic extent $L$ and wave number $k_j$ and the scale regime $k_jL\ll1$; no error bound is supplied. A rotating-wave choice keeps only the excitation-exchange terms. For a two-level transition of frequency $\omega_0$ coupled to a mode of frequency $\omega$, its usual low-excitation regime is $|g|\sqrt{n+1}\ll\omega,\omega_0$ on the declared photon-number sectors; it is not uniform over the full Fock space. A Markov/GKSL approximation is another separate model choice and must state its rates, reservoir correlation time $\tau_B$, system time scale $\tau_S$, and regime $\tau_B\ll\tau_S$. None of these optional approximations is derived from this assignment or from the finite system-environment model.

items.physical_scope: An adopted effective model assignment for finitely many bosonic oscillator modes coupled to a finite atomic Hilbert space, together with explicitly selected ideal photon-counting and homodyne outcome models. It asserts no laboratory mode content, detector realization, measured coupling, controlled truncation error, continuum spontaneous-emission law, QED photon localization, photon position or spin tensor decomposition, helicity, angular-momentum split, or paraxial limit. Long-wavelength, rotating-wave and Markov regimes are optional, separately stated approximations.

items.title: Ideal single-mode normally ordered second factorial statistic
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement: Specialize the finite-mode assignment to $M=1$, identify the coordinate vector $(z)\in\mathbb C^1$ with its single component $z\in\mathbb C$, and write $\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C)$ for this one-mode Fock space. Write $|n\rangle$ for the occupation vector with $n$ quanta in its unique mode. Let $\rho$ be a density operator (a positive trace-class operator of trace one) on $\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C)$. Let $\Pi_n:=|n\rangle\langle n|$ be the ideal number-count PVM, with probabilities $p_n:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho\Pi_n)$. Suppose $\bar n:=\sum_{n\ge0}np_n$ is finite and strictly positive, and $m_2:=\sum_{n\ge0}n(n-1)p_n$ is finite. Define the model's equal-time second factorial statistic by $g^{(2)}(0;\rho):=m_2/\bar n^2$. On finite-particle number vectors the one-mode maps satisfy $a|0\rangle=0$, $a|n\rangle=\sqrt n|n-1\rangle$ for $n\ge1$, and $a^*|n\rangle=\sqrt{n+1}|n+1\rangle$ for $n\ge0$. Normal ordering here means placing creation maps to the left of annihilation maps; these actions give $a^*a^*aa|n\rangle=n(n-1)|n\rangle$ for $n\ge0$. Thus $m_2$ is the corresponding number-basis factorial moment, defined here directly by its probability sum rather than by an unqualified expectation of an unbounded operator product. This uses only the ideal counting model; it asserts no time-resolved photocurrent law, empirical detection, or detector realization.

references.title: Carlos Navarrete-Benlloch, Introduction to Quantum Optics, full lecture notes, §VI.2.1
references.locator: Equation (491) and footnote 51 define normal ordering for output photodetection correlations; that continuous-time open-system correlation model is not imported here.

references.title: Christian Weedbrook et al., Gaussian Quantum Information, §II.5.4
references.locator: The number-basis PVM E_n=|n><n| and the distinction between ideal number measurement and inefficient avalanche detection.

items.physical_scope: The dimensionless equal-time second factorial statistic in the one-mode specialization of the finite-mode assignment, under an ideal number-resolving count model. It is a model-defined normal-ordered moment for states with finite moments and positive mean number. No multimode output-field correlation, finite-trial observation, detector response, or laboratory antibunching result is asserted.

items.title: Jaynes–Cummings invariant blocks and Rabi frequency
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Take the one-mode, two-level specialization of the finite-mode assignment and use its SI convention with $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds. Let $\omega>0$ be the selected angular frequency in seconds$^{-1}$, let $\mathcal H_A=\mathbb C^2$ have orthonormal states $|g\rangle,|e\rangle$, and choose $\omega_0>0$ in seconds$^{-1}$, $d\in\mathbb R$ in coulomb-metres, and $\mathcal E\in\mathbb R$ in volts per metre. Set $\sigma_+=|e\rangle\langle g|$, $\sigma_-=|g\rangle\langle e|$, $\sigma_z=|e\rangle\langle e|-|g\rangle\langle g|$, and $\sigma_x=\sigma_++\sigma_-$. Choose $H_A=(\hbar\omega_0/2)\sigma_z$ and $D=d\sigma_x$; then the dipole expression $-\mathcal E D\otimes(a+a^*)$ has energy units. Define the real coupling $g:=-\mathcal E d/\hbar$ in seconds$^{-1}$. Retaining from the dipole expression just the excitation-exchange terms $\sigma_+\otimes a$ and $\sigma_-\otimes a^*$ gives coefficient $-\mathcal E d=\hbar g$. Thus the rotating-wave Hamiltonian below is a specified specialization of the model assignment, not an independently measured interaction.

Let $\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C)$ be the infinite-dimensional one-mode bosonic Fock space with occupation basis $|n\rangle$, $n\in\mathbb N_0$, and operators $a|n\rangle=\sqrt n|n-1\rangle$, $a^*|n\rangle=\sqrt{n+1}|n+1\rangle$ on the finite-particle core. Write $I_A$ and $I_F$ for the identity operators on the atomic and field factors, respectively. Define $\Delta=\omega_0-\omega$. For this rotating-wave model, whose usual scale $|g|\sqrt{n+1}\ll\omega,\omega_0$ applies only to the photon-number sectors under study and is not uniform over the full Fock space, set
$$H_{\rm core}=\hbar\omega\,I_A\otimes a^*a+\frac{\hbar\omega_0}{2}\sigma_z\otimes I_F+\hbar g(\sigma_+\otimes a+\sigma_-\otimes a^*)$$
on the finite-particle core of $\mathbb C^2\widehat\otimes\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C)$. The Hamiltonian is the exact operator for the selected rotating-wave model; no error bound relative to the unapproximated dipole interaction is asserted.

The total excitation operator $N_{\rm exc}:=I_A\otimes a^*a+\sigma_+\sigma_-\otimes I_F$ is conserved on that core. The ground line $\mathbb C|g,0\rangle$ is invariant. For each $n\in\mathbb N_0$, the subspace $\mathcal K_n=\operatorname{span}\{|e,n\rangle,|g,n+1\rangle\}$ is invariant and the restriction has matrix
$$H_n=\begin{pmatrix}\hbar\omega n+\frac{\hbar\omega_0}{2}&\hbar g\sqrt{n+1}\\\hbar g\sqrt{n+1}&\hbar\omega(n+1)-\frac{\hbar\omega_0}{2}\end{pmatrix}.$$
Its eigenvalue splitting is $\hbar\sqrt{\Delta^2+4g^2(n+1)}$. Define the full Hamiltonian to act on the ground line by $-\hbar\omega_0/2$ and as the orthogonal direct sum of the $H_n$ on the $\mathcal K_n$, with squared-block-norm domain
$$D(H_{\rm JC})=\left\{c|g,0\rangle\oplus\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\psi_n:\ c\in\mathbb C,\ \psi_n\in\mathcal K_n,\ \sum_{n\ge0}\|H_n\psi_n\|^2<\infty\right\}.$$
This direct-sum operator is self-adjoint and extends $H_{\rm core}$.

references.title: Carlos Navarrete-Benlloch, Introduction to Quantum Optics, full lecture notes, §§IV.2.1–2.2
references.locator: The rotating-wave Jaynes–Cummings Hamiltonian and excitation sectors, Eqs. (267)–(271). The local proof fixes a different coupling phase and completes the operator-domain argument.

items.physical_scope: An exact conditional calculation for the single-mode, two-level rotating-wave model on the full infinite-dimensional oscillator Fock space. The excitation blocks and self-adjoint direct-sum realization are model deductions. The usual weak-coupling rotating-wave scale condition is not uniform over all Fock states; no continuum spontaneous-emission law, detector observation, or laboratory identification is asserted.

items.title: Passive beam-splitter photon statistics
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Assume the finite-mode assignment with two modes and its ideal number PVM, with AC and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as required by the implementer and completed Fock/tensor suppliers. Write $\mathcal F^{(2)}=\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C^2)$ in the ordered mode basis $(1,0),(0,1)$ and $\mathcal F=\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C)$. The mode-factorization map is the unitary $\mathcal J:\mathcal F^{(2)}\to\mathcal F\widehat\otimes\mathcal F$ determined by $\mathcal J|m,n\rangle=|m\rangle\otimes|n\rangle$. Here $\widehat\otimes$ is the completed Hilbert tensor product, and the one-mode occupation vectors and their products use the same vacuum and mode order. Its unitary extension is proved below. Let $t,r\in\mathbb C$ be dimensionless amplitudes with $|t|^2+|r|^2=1$, and fix the complete unitary mode matrix $C=\begin{pmatrix}t&-\overline r\\r&\overline t\end{pmatrix}$. Use the state-action convention that the passive unitary $U_C$ satisfies $U_C\Omega=\Omega$, $U_Ca_1^*U_C^*=t a_1^*+r a_2^*$, and $U_Ca_2^*U_C^*=-\overline r\,a_1^*+\overline t\,a_2^*$ on the finite-particle core. Put $\eta:=|t|^2$. For $n\in\mathbb N_0$ and $0\le k\le n$, write $\binom nk:=n!/(k!(n-k)!)$. For input $|n,0\rangle$ and $0<\eta<1$, the joint output count law is
$$\mathbb P(k,\ell)=\begin{cases}\binom nk\eta^k(1-\eta)^{n-k},&\ell=n-k,\ 0\le k\le n,\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}$$
At $\eta=0$ and $\eta=1$ the joint laws are respectively point masses at $(0,n)$ and $(n,0)$. Thus the first output count is binomial with parameters $(n,\eta)$. For a dimensionless coherent input $|\alpha,0\rangle$ with $|\alpha\rangle=e^{-|\alpha|^2/2}\sum_{n\ge0}\alpha^n|n\rangle/\sqrt{n!}$, define $|\alpha,0\rangle=\mathcal J^*(|\alpha\rangle\otimes|0\rangle)$, equivalently $e^{-|\alpha|^2/2}\sum_{n\ge0}\alpha^n|n,0\rangle/\sqrt{n!}$. The output state under this fixed mode factorization is $\mathcal J U_C|\alpha,0\rangle=|t\alpha\rangle\otimes|r\alpha\rangle$; on $\mathcal F^{(2)}$ it is $\mathcal J^*(|t\alpha\rangle\otimes|r\alpha\rangle)$.

references.title: Christian Weedbrook et al., Gaussian Quantum Information, §II.2.6
references.locator: The two-mode beam-splitter unitary and Heisenberg matrix, Eqs. (36)–(38); the item fixes its own state-action/port phase convention.

items.physical_scope: An exact two-mode passive-unitary model calculation in the infinite-dimensional finite-mode bosonic Fock space, with ideal number-resolving outcomes. It gives conditional count distributions for specified number and coherent inputs. The result is not an experiment or a claim that an actual optical device realizes the assigned unitary.

items.title: Pure loss channel and binomial thinning
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Assume AC and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the assigned finite-mode model, one input mode and a second mode prepared independently in vacuum $|0\rangle\langle0|$. Write $\mathcal F:=\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C)$ for each one-mode Fock space and $\mathcal F^{(2)}:=\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C^2)$ for the two-mode Fock space with ordered coordinate basis $e_1=(1,0),e_2=(0,1)$. In the completed product $\mathcal F\widehat\otimes\mathcal F$, define $\mathcal I(|m\rangle\otimes|n\rangle):=|m,n\rangle$ on occupation vectors, where $|m,n\rangle$ is the two-mode occupation basis in that ordered mode basis. The product-basis result and finite-mode Fock occupation-basis result listed in Statement references make $\mathcal I$ extend uniquely to a unitary $\mathcal I:\mathcal F\widehat\otimes\mathcal F\to\mathcal F^{(2)}$. For $0\le\eta\le1$, define $C_\eta:=\begin{pmatrix}\sqrt\eta&-\sqrt{1-\eta}\\\sqrt{1-\eta}&\sqrt\eta\end{pmatrix}$ and let $U_\eta:=U_{C_\eta}$ be the two-mode beam-splitter unitary specified by the beam-splitter result in Statement references on $\mathcal F^{(2)}$. Transport this unitary to the product space as $\widetilde U_\eta:=\mathcal I^*U_\eta\mathcal I$. Define the vacuum insertion isometry $V_0:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F\widehat\otimes\mathcal F$ by $V_0\psi=\psi\otimes|0\rangle$. For every trace-class operator $\rho$ on $\mathcal F$, the vacuum product operator $\rho\otimes|0\rangle\langle0|$ means $V_0\rho V_0^*$, a trace-class operator by the trace-class ideal and tensor-map suppliers. Define
$$\Phi_\eta(\rho):=\operatorname{Tr}_2\!\left(\widetilde U_\eta(\rho\otimes|0\rangle\langle0|)\widetilde U_\eta^*\right),$$
where $\operatorname{Tr}_2$ is the trace-class partial trace over the second one-mode factor. Here CPTP means complex-linear, trace-preserving, and positive after every finite-dimensional ancilla amplification on trace-class operators. The map $\Phi_\eta$ is CPTP. For $0<\eta<1$ and an input number state $|n\rangle$, its output state is
$$\Phi_\eta(|n\rangle\langle n|)=\sum_{k=0}^n\binom nk\eta^k(1-\eta)^{n-k}|k\rangle\langle k|,$$
so ideal number detection has the binomial-thinning law. At $\eta=0$ this number input is mapped to vacuum, and at $\eta=1$ it is unchanged. For a coherent input $|\alpha\rangle$, its output is $|\sqrt\eta\,\alpha\rangle\langle\sqrt\eta\,\alpha|$ for every $0\le\eta\le1$. On arbitrary input states, $\Phi_0$ maps to vacuum and $\Phi_1$ is the identity.

references.title: Christian Weedbrook et al., Gaussian Quantum Information, §§II.2.6 and V.2
references.locator: §II.2.6, Eqs. (36)–(38), defines passive beam-splitter mixing; §V.2, the pure-loss case is a beam splitter mixing the signal with vacuum. The local proof establishes trace-class CPTP and the stated number/coherent outputs.

references.title: Carlos Navarrete-Benlloch, Introduction to Quantum Optics, full lecture notes, §§II and IV.2
references.locator: Finite oscillator Fock modes and single-mode light–matter model conventions; no continuum or detector-data result is imported.

items.physical_scope: An exact conditional one-mode pure-loss model with a vacuum environment mode, a passive two-mode unitary and a trace over the environment. The channel, binomial thinning and coherent-state attenuation are model deductions on the full infinite-dimensional finite-mode Fock space. No detector efficiency, actual loss record, apparatus realization, continuum bath, weak-coupling limit or experimental data are asserted.

title: Finite-mode light–matter models and detection statistics — Examples

items.title: Vacuum Rabi oscillation
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement: In the resonant Jaynes–Cummings model ($\omega_0=\omega$), prepare the atom and field in $|e,0\rangle$ and let the ideal model evolve for time $\tau\ge0$. The assigned excited-state PVM then gives excitation probability $\cos^2(g\tau)$. If $g\ne0$, the population returns to one at $\tau=k\pi/|g|$, $k\in\mathbb N_0$; if $g=0$, it remains one. This is a periodic model prediction, not irreversible spontaneous decay or a reported observation.

references.title: Carlos Navarrete-Benlloch, Introduction to Quantum Optics, full lecture notes, §IV.2.2
references.locator: Jaynes–Cummings invariant excitation sectors and dressed-state blocks, Eqs. (268)–(271); the local example computes the vacuum block independently.

items.physical_scope: A conditional single-excitation calculation in the ideal closed Jaynes–Cummings two-level, one-mode rotating-wave model. It predicts periodic excitation transfer and revival within that model, not irreversible decay or continuum spontaneous emission. No measured oscillation or apparatus record is asserted.

items.title: Ideal single-mode factorial moment
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement: For the one-mode number state $|1\rangle$ and the ideal number-count model, the mean number is $\langle a^*a\rangle=1$ while the normally ordered second factorial moment is $\langle a^*a^*aa\rangle=0$, so the assigned $g^{(2)}(0)$ statistic is zero. If the input $|1,0\rangle$ is mixed with vacuum at the declared passive beam splitter, its output has exactly one total count, split between the two ports with probabilities $\eta$ and $1-\eta$. These are model predictions only; no detector realization or experimental antibunching record is asserted.

references.locator: Equation (491) and footnote 51 explain normal ordering in photodetection correlations; no output-field data or open-system formula is imported.

references.title: Christian Weedbrook et al., Gaussian Quantum Information, §§II.2.6 and II.5.4
references.locator: Passive beam splitter transformation and ideal number-basis PVM; the local result is a finite-mode state calculation.

items.physical_scope: An ideal one-quantum Fock-state calculation of a single-mode normal-ordered factorial statistic and its passive beam-splitter count distribution. This is a conditional finite-mode model prediction, not a detector observation or experimental antibunching dataset.
